All the questions in Part A and any three questions in Part B.
Questions in Part A carry 10 marks each and questions in Part B cany 20 marks each.
1. Discuss how the friendship between Lionel Verney and Adrian contributes to the themes of companionship and loss.
Discuss the complex delineation of race and racial superiority in The
Last Man.
2. In what ways does The Time Machine critically engage with Darwin's Theory of Evolution.
How does The Time Machine reflect H.G. Wells' critique of late Victorian social class divisions ?
3. Comment on the following extract.
"Bigger the population, the more minorities. Don't step on the toes of the dog lovers, the cat lovers, doctors, lawyers, merchants, chiefs, Mormons, Baptists,
Unitarians, second-generation Chinese, Swedes, Italians, Germans, Texans,
Brooklynites, Irishmen, people from Oregon or Mexico. The people in this book, this play, this TV serial are not meant to represent any actual painters, cartographers, mechanics anywhere. The bigger your market, Montag, the less you handle controversy, remember that!... Authors, full of evil thoughts, lock up your typewriters. They did."
Critically examine the character of Clarisse McClellan in
4. Examine the social world represented by Mary Shelley in light of the collapse of human ambition and society.
Nature has a complex role in the novel both as a source of beauty and as a destructive element. Comment on interaction between nature and human society in The Last Man.
Discuss The Time Machine as a dystopian text.
6. Critically examine the contrasting relationships Montag shares with Captain
Beatty and Professor Faber in Fahrenheit 451. How do these two figures represent opposing ideologies, and in what ways do they shape Montag's psychological and moral transformation over the course of the novel ?
Referring to the line "If you don't want a man unhappy politically, don't give him two sides to a question to worry him; give him one. Better yet, give him none," critically analyse how Fahrenheit 451 constructs its dystopian world.
How does Bradbury use elements such as censorship, conformity and technological control to portray a society that suppresses critical thought and emotional depth ?
7. What is the role of individuality in dystopian writings ? Elucidate with reference to any text in your syllabus.
Comment on the popular and effective metaphors employed by writers of dystopian literature to represent the calamitous possibilities of the future.

2038182011.text:
Type of the Paper : DSE
Candidates have to answer all the questions in Part A and any three questions in Part B.
Questions in Part A carry 10 marks each and questions in Part B cárry 20 marks cach.
In the context of political communication, how do politicians use social media platforms to shape public opinion and influence electoral outcomes ?
Analyse the complex relationship between religion and politics in India, highlighting how religious identities and ideologies influence electoral outcomes and policy decisions.
What is packaging politics and how does it impact political campaigning and election outcomes ?
How do politicians utilize language as a tool to shape public opinion, influence voter attitudes and advance their agendas ?
3. Discuss the use of emotional appeals in political advertising with suitable examples.
How do social movements utilize language and rhetoric to mobilize support and exacerbate polarization ? What are the implications of this for democratic discourse and societal cohesion ?
4. Discuss the strategies that can be employed to promote greater representation and inclusion of women in political leadership.
How do cultural identities, values and practices shape political attitudes, behaviours and outcomes and what are the implications for democratic governance and social cohesion in diverse societies?
5. What are common rhetorical strategies to shape public opinion, influence voter attitudes and advance agendas ? Discuss with relevant examples.
What strategies can be employed to promote fact-based reasoning and critical thinking in the face of misinformation and disinformation in politics ?
How do social media platforms shape political engagement, influence public opinion and impact civic participation ?
How is AI being used in politics and what are the potential implications for democracy and civic engagement ?
7 How do comedians, satirists and politicians use humour to critique power and shape cultural narratives ?
Examine the complex relationship between politics and media, discussing how media shapes public opinion, influences political discourse and impacts the exercise of power.
